Increased traffic created by commuting mine employees and the larger area population would impact existing roads at all levels of production. Congestion will increase, more traffic accidents will occur and road deterioration will accelerate. The expected increased tax base will aid county government in improvement and reconstruction of inadequate road systems. A problem may arise if this tax base is not realized concurrent with the need for new road systems.
Neither the short railroad spur to be constructed at the high level of production, nor addition of small sections of transmission lines are expected to significantly impact the existing transportation facilities.
Increased automobile, truck, and railroad traffic will dramatically upset the rural character of this area.
Air traffic to the Hardin airport would increase, possibly calling for improvements in the landing strip and facilities. It is anticipated, however, that the bulk of additional air traffic would be noticed at Billings, where it could be handled easily.
Municipal Services - The four communities studied in the impact area are all projected to receive significant but consistent population growth and an associated increase in demand for city services. In three of the communities, Wyola, Lodge Grass, and Crow Agency, this increase in demand will be due almost entirely to natural population increase, particularly that of the Crow Indians. Therefore the demand for services will increase at a steady rate during the 25 year study period. The present level of services in each of these towns is either at capacity or rapidly reaching capacity, so in the immediate future all towns will be faced with increasing their services, as shown in Table III-6.
